newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia privatises 204 of its 326 state-run firms.
newsitem.headline: Zambia privatises 204 of its 326 state-run firms.

text.p: Zambia has sold 204 of a total of 326 state-run enterprises since it embarked on a privatisation programme four years ago, the Zambia Privatisation Agency (ZPA) said on Wednesday.

"A total of 204 companies have been privatised and another 34 companies are ready for privatisation or under negotiation. Forty three others are under preparation for privatisation," a company official told Reuters.
The official said 25 companies would be liquidated or would undergo asset sales, while the sale of eight others was being held up by legal actions.
"One company is undergoing pre-privatisation preparation while 11 others are not being handled by ZPA," the official said.
The Frederick Chiluba government started selling off state-run enterprises in 1993 as part of reforms to turn the economy around.

The government expects to sell off by year-end assets belonging to the Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM), the mining conglomerate responsible for about 90 percent of the country's foreign receipts.
Another major company due for privatisation is the Zambia Telecommunications Company Ltd, which is being prepared for privatisation.
